items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022
items.q: I went to Jill Goodwin and I borrowed a tape recorder

ctx.x: Well I didn’t really hear jazz on the radio. I didn’t listen to the radio at that age. My brother, older brother, was a waiter at a camp in Western Massachusetts one summer and he stole the George Shearing album, without the cover, and brought it back to me, thinking I would enjoy it. That’s the first jazz I ever heard. It was called “Changing With the Times.” And there was that tune on “Changing With the Times” was on there. I knew when I got the record, I thought this is it. I knew — I recognized this is what I…

“George,” I went up and I told him I says, “you’re the cause I’m here today” you know because your record was the first record, jazz record I ever heard. As a matter of fact, well I’ll tell you more about that later. So I says, “George, there was a tune on that record called ‘Changing With the Times’ that I tried to copy and I never could get it.” He said, “Well, Hal,” he says, “boy that’s a long time ago” he says, “give me a couple of days to think about it” you know. I said okay. So we were in a different place…
How would you like to share that?
